title: Regular -ER and -IR verbs in the preterite
summary: One set of endings for both -er and -ir verbs: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron.
focus: Preterite (pretérito indefinido) of regular -er and -ir verbs
content:
## One set of endings for -er and -ir

In the preterite, **-er** and **-ir** verbs share the same endings. Remove **-er** or **-ir** and add:

| person | ending | comer | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | **-í** | com**í** | viv**í** |
| tú | **-iste** | com**iste** | viv**iste** |
| él / ella / usted | **-ió** | com**ió** | viv**ió** |
| nosotros/as | **-imos** | com**imos** | viv**imos** |
| vosotros/as | **-isteis** | com**isteis** | viv**isteis** |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **-ieron** | com**ieron** | viv**ieron** |

- *Ayer comí paella.* (Yesterday I ate paella.)
- *Salieron a las diez.* (They went out at ten.)
- *¿Escribiste el correo?* (Did you write the email?)

## Watch the accents: comí, comió

As with **-ar** verbs, the **yo** and **él/ella/usted** forms carry a written accent: **-í** and **-ió**. It separates past from present:

- *vivo* = I live vs. *vivió* = he/she lived
- *como* = I eat vs. *comí* = I ate

The other forms have **no** accent: *comimos*, *vivimos*, *salisteis*.

For **-ir** verbs the **nosotros** form looks the same as the present: *vivimos* = we live / we lived. For **-er** verbs it differs: *comemos* (we eat) vs. *comimos* (we ate).

## Time markers for the past

The preterite usually comes with a time marker that fixes the action in the past:

- **ayer**: *Ayer bebí demasiado café.* (Yesterday I drank too much coffee.)
- **anoche**: *Anoche salimos con unos amigos.* (Last night we went out with some friends.)
- **la semana pasada**: *La semana pasada escribí tres correos.* (Last week I wrote three emails.)
- **el año pasado**: *El año pasado vivimos en Valencia.* (Last year we lived in Valencia.)
- **hace dos días**: *Hace dos días aprendí la palabra.* (Two days ago I learnt the word.)

**Hace** + a length of time means *ago*: *hace una hora*, *hace tres años*.

## A spelling note: leer → leyó

When the stem ends in a vowel (**leer**, **creer**, **oír**), the **i** of **-ió** and **-ieron** turns into a **y** so that it does not sit between two vowels:

- leer → *leyó*, *leyeron* (but *leí*, *leíste*, *leímos*)
- creer → *creyó*, *creyeron*

Just recognise these for now. Drill the regular endings.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Yesterday we ate paella on the beach.
Last night I drank too much coffee.
I lived in Madrid for three years.

vocabulary.example: Salieron a las diez de la noche.
vocabulary.example_meaning: They went out at ten at night.
I learned a lot in the course.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Last year we lived in Valencia.

vocabulary.example_meaning: Two days ago I went out with my friends.

What did you eat at the weekend?

quiz.explanation: The yo ending for -er and -ir verbs is -í with an accent: 'comí'.

quiz.prompt: Anoche Marta ___ un correo a su jefe.
quiz.explanation: Marta = ella, which takes -ió in the preterite: 'escribió'. 'Escribo' is present tense 'I write'.
Nosotros takes -imos: 'vivimos'. For -ir verbs it looks exactly like the present; no accent.
hints: Same as the present for -ir verbs.

quiz.explanation: Vosotros takes -isteis: 'salisteis'. 'Saliste' is tú, 'salieron' is ellos.

quiz.prompt: Hace dos días mis amigos ___ (beber) demasiado café.
quiz.explanation: 'Mis amigos' = ellos, which takes -ieron: 'bebieron'. 'Hace dos días' means two days ago.

quiz.prompt: El año pasado yo ___ mucho en el curso.
quiz.explanation: Yo takes -í in the preterite: 'aprendí'. 'Aprendió' is he/she, 'aprendo' is present.
hints: 'El año pasado' puts it in the past.

quiz.explanation: Tú takes -iste: 'comiste'. There is no extra -s at the end.

quiz.prompt: Which sentence means 'She read the book'?
quiz.explanation: The stem of leer ends in a vowel, so the i of -ió becomes y: 'leyó'. 'Leímos' is we, 'lee' is present.

quiz.prompt: Ayer nosotros ___ (comer) paella en la playa.
quiz.explanation: Nosotros takes -imos: 'comimos'. Note the difference from the present 'comemos'.
hints: The present has -emos; the preterite swaps the e for an i.

listening.note: Yo form: accent on the final í.

listening.meaning: Did you write the email yesterday?

listening.text: Anoche salimos del cine a las once.
listening.meaning: Last night we left the cinema at eleven.
listening.note: Salimos is present or past; anoche makes it past.

listening.text: Hace dos días aprendí una canción nueva.
listening.meaning: Two days ago I learnt a new song.
listening.note: New word: la canción = the song.

listening.text: ¿A qué hora salisteis del curso ayer?
listening.meaning: What time did you all leave the class yesterday?

listening.text: El fin de semana bebimos demasiado vino en la boda.
listening.meaning: At the weekend we drank too much wine at the wedding.
listening.note: New word: la boda = the wedding.

listening.text: El año pasado mi hermano vivió en Alemania y aprendió alemán.
listening.meaning: Last year my brother lived in Germany and learnt German.

guide.tip: Hear the stress: comÍ, comIÓ at the end; comISte, comIMos in the middle. Only the end-stressed forms get a written accent.

conversations.title: Dinner last night
conversations.scenario: Carmen and Pablo meet at the bus stop and talk about what they did last night and last year.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Hi, Pablo. Did you go out last night?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, salí con mis compañeros del curso. Comimos en un restaurante italiano.
lines.meaning: Yes, I went out with my classmates from the course. We ate at an Italian restaurant.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Yo comí pasta y los demás comieron pizza. Bebimos demasiado vino, la verdad.
lines.meaning: I ate pasta and the others ate pizza. We drank too much wine, to be honest.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Ha! What time did you get back home?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Volví a la una. Y tú, ¿qué hiciste? ¿Escribiste el correo a tu jefe?
lines.meaning: I got back at one. And you, what did you do? Did you write the email to your boss?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, lo escribí anoche. Después leí un poco y me dormí temprano.
lines.meaning: Yes, I wrote it last night. Afterwards I read a little and fell asleep early.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Oye, tú viviste en Italia, ¿no? ¿Aprendiste italiano allí?
lines.meaning: Hey, you lived in Italy, right? Did you learn Italian there?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Sí, viví dos años en Roma. Aprendí mucho, pero el año pasado volví a España.
lines.meaning: Yes, I lived in Rome for two years. I learnt a lot, but last year I came back to Spain.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¡Qué suerte! Mis padres vivieron en Lisboa hace muchos años.
lines.meaning: Lucky you! My parents lived in Lisbon many years ago.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Bueno, ahí viene el autobús. ¡Hasta luego!
lines.meaning: Well, here comes the bus. See you later!

bites.title: One set for two families
bites.rule: -er and -ir verbs share the same preterite endings: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. Learn one set and you know both.
bites.example: Comí paella y viví en Valencia.
bites.example_meaning: I ate paella and I lived in Valencia.

bites.title: Accent on í and ió
bites.rule: Yo -í and él/ella -ió carry the accent; vivo = I live, vivió = he lived. The other four forms have no accent.

bites.title: Pin it in time
bites.rule: Ayer, anoche, la semana pasada, el año pasado and hace dos días (two days ago) all call for the preterite. Hace + time = ago.
bites.example: Hace dos días salí con mis amigos.
bites.example_meaning: Two days ago I went out with my friends.

bites.title: leer → leyó
bites.rule: When the stem ends in a vowel (leer, creer), -ió and -ieron become -yó and -yeron: leyó, leyeron, creyó. Just recognise them for now.
bites.example_meaning: She read the book last night.

sorts.title: Present or past?
sorts.why: The accented -í/-ió and the -iste, -imos endings mark the preterite; -o, -es and -emos are present.

sorts.title: Accent or no accent?
sorts.why: Only yo (-í) and él/ella (-ió) take a written accent.

spots.sentence: Ayer yo comó paella con mi familia.
spots.why: -er and -ir verbs take -í in the yo form, never -ó: comí.

spots.sentence: Anoche Marta escribó un correo a su jefe.

spots.why: The tú preterite ends in -iste, with no final s.

spots.sentence: El año pasado vivímos en Valencia.
spots.why: Nosotros -imos has no written accent: vivimos.

spots.sentence: Hace dos días mis amigos bebimos demasiado café.
spots.why: Mis amigos = ellos, which takes -ieron: bebieron.

spots.sentence: Ella leió el libro en dos días.
spots.why: After a vowel the i of -ió becomes y: leyó.
